1.1: And it came to pass, when the king of the Chaldeans had taken the children of Israel captive, that the Lord spoke to Jeremiah, saying:
1.2: Jeremiah, my chosen, arise and go forth out of this city, you and Baruch; for I will destroy it because of the multitude of the sins of them that dwell in it. For your prayer is as a strong pillar in the midst of the city, and as a wall of adamant round about it. Now therefore arise you, and go and depart, before the host of the Chaldeans come and compass the city.
1.3: And Jeremiah answered, saying: "I beseech you, my Lord, suffer your servant to speak before you."
1.4: And the Lord said to him: "Speak, my chosen Jeremiah."
1.5: And Jeremiah answered and said: "O Lord of all, will you deliver this chosen city into the hands of the Chaldeans, that the king with his people may boast and say, I have prevailed against the city of God?"
1.6: No, my Lord; but if it please you, destroy it with your own hands.
1.7: And the Lord said to Jeremiah: "Because you are my chosen, arise and go forth, you and Baruch; for I will destroy it because of the sins of them that dwell in it. And neither the king nor his host shall be able to enter into the city, except I first open and enlarge the gates of it."
1.8: Arise now, and go to Baruch, and tell him this word; and when the sixth hour of the night has come, enter you within the walls of the city, and I will show you: for except I first destroy the city, they shall not be able to enter into it.
1.9: And when the Lord had spoken these things, he departed from Jeremiah.

2.1: And Jeremiah rent his garments, and cast ashes upon his head, and entered into the house of the sanctuary.
2.2: And Baruch saw Jeremiah [with] ashes strewn upon his head, and his garments rent; and he cried with a loud voice, saying: "My father Jeremiah, what ails you? and what sin have the people committed? For when the people sinned, Jeremiah mourned, and cast ashes upon his head, and prayed for the people, that their iniquity might be forgiven them."
2.3: And Baruch asked him, saying: My father Jeremiah, what ails you, and what has become of the people?
2.4: And Jeremiah said to him: "Take heed that we rend not our garments, but let us rend our hearts; and let us put no water into the basins, that we may weep bitterly until we fill them with our tears: for from henceforth he will have no mercy on this people."
2.5: And Baruch said: "My father Jeremiah, what ails you?"
2.6: And Jeremiah said to him: "God will deliver the city into the hand of the king of the Chaldeans; for he shall lead the people captive in affliction."
2.7: And when Baruch heard all this, he rent his garments, and said: "My father Jeremiah, who has showed you this?"
2.8: And Jeremiah said to him: "Abide with me until the sixth hour of the night, that you may know that the word is true."
2.9: And they abode in the house of the sanctuary, weeping.

3.1: And when the sixth hour of the night was come, whereof the Lord had told Jeremiah, that he should go up with Baruch, they went up within the walls of the city, and abode watching.
3.2: And there was the sound of a trumpet, and angels came forth from heaven, holding torches of fire in their hands, and stood within the walls of the city.
3.3: And when Jeremiah and Baruch saw them, they wept, saying: Now we know that the word is true.
3.4: And Jeremiah besought the angels, saying: I beseech you all, destroy not the city, until I ask one word of the Lord;
3.5: And the Lord answered the angels, saying: "Destroy not the city, until I speak with Jeremiah my chosen."
3.6: Then spoke Jeremiah, saying: "I beseech you, my Lord, give me leave to speak with you. And he said to him: Speak, my chosen Jeremiah, whatsoever you will."
3.7: And Jeremiah said to him: "Behold, now we know, my Lord, that you will deliver the city into the hand of the enemy, and the people shall be carried away to Babylon. What will you that I do with the holy vessels of our ministry, which you have committed to us? and what will you that I do concerning them?"
3.8: And the Lord said to him: "Take them, and commit them to the earth, and to the house of the sanctuary, saying:"
3.9: And you, O earth, hear the voice of your Creator, who formed you in the abundance of waters, who sealed you with seven seals: take again your beauty, and guard the vessels of your ministry until the coming of the Beloved.
3.10: And Jeremiah answered and said: "I beseech you, my Lord, show me what I shall do for Abimelech the Ethiopian; for he has done many kindnesses to the people and to your servant Jeremiah: he was distinguished above all the men of the city, and he drew me out of the miry pit; and I would not that he should see the destruction and desolation of the city, lest he be grieved."
3.11: And the Lord said to Jeremiah: "Send him into the vineyard of Agrippa, by the mountain way; and I will hide him, until I bring the people again into the city;"
3.12: And you, Jeremiah, go with the people until you come to the land of Babylon, and abide prophesying to them, until I bring them into their city;
3.13: But leave you Baruch here in Jerusalem.
3.14: And when the Lord had spoken all this to Jeremiah, he departed from Jeremiah into heaven.
3.15: And Jeremiah and Baruch entered into the house of the sanctuary, and committed all the vessels of their ministry to the earth, as the Lord had commanded them; and straightway the earth swallowed them, and they twain abode and wept.
3.16: And in the morning Jeremiah sent Abimelech, saying: Take a basket, and go by the mountain way into the vineyard of Agrippa, and bring a few figs for the sick of the people; for the favor of the Lord is upon your head, and his glory. And he went as he commanded him.

4.1: And in the morning the host of the Chaldeans compassed the city; and a great angel blew the trumpet, saying: Enter you, O host of the Chaldeans; behold, the gates are opened to you.
4.2: Then the king entered with his army, and they took all the people captive.
4.3: And then Jeremiah took the keys of the house of the sanctuary, and went forth out of the city, and cast these keys before the sun, saying: To you I speak, O sun: take the keys of the house of God, and keep them until the day in which the Lord shall require them of you; for we were not found worthy to keep them, for we have been found unfaithful in our sins.
4.4: And while Jeremiah was yet weeping for the people, they brought him forth and dragged him, and led him away with the people to Babylon.
4.5: But Baruch took ashes and cast them upon his head, and abode and wailed this wailing, saying:
4.6: Why is Jerusalem made desolate? but for the sin of the beloved people was she delivered into the hand of her enemies, for our sins and for the sins of the people;
4.7: But let not the sinners boast, neither let them say: We were able to take the city of God by our might; it was not by your strength that you prevailed against her, but for our sins was she delivered to you;
4.8: And our God will have mercy upon us, and bring us again into our city; but as for you, there shall be no life. Blessed are our fathers, Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob; for they departed out of this world, and saw not the destruction of this city.
4.9: And after he had spoken this, he went forth weeping, and said: "I mourn for you, O Jerusalem. And he went out of the city, and abode in a tomb; and the angels came to him, and showed him concerning all things."

5.1: And Abimelech took the figs at the time of midday, as Jeremiah had sent him; and he found a shady tree, and abode and rested, to take a little rest; and he leaned his head upon the basket of figs, and slept sixty and six years, and awoke not from his sleep.
5.2: And after a time he arose and awoke from his sleep, and said: "I have slept sweetly a little while; for my head is heavy, and I have not had my fill of sleep."
5.3: And he uncovered that basket of figs, and found the figs fresh, and their milk dripping.
5.4: And he desired to sleep again, for his head was heavy, and he was not sated with slumber; and he said: "I fear lest I sleep and be late, lest my father Jeremiah rebuke me; for he sent me early in the morning. And now I will arise and go; for is there not heat, is there not toil, every day?"
5.5: And he arose, and took up the basket of his figs, and entered into the city Jerusalem; and he knew not the city, nor his house. And he said: "Blessed are you, O Lord; for a great trance is fallen upon me."
5.6: And he said: "Is this indeed the city Jerusalem? I have surely gone astray, for I came by the mountain way; and if my head be heavy and I have not had my fill of sleep, my heart is perplexed within me; and how shall I declare this thing to Jeremiah, that the city is hidden from me?"
5.7: And he sought out all the landmarks that were in the city, to know whether this were Jerusalem. And he went again into the city, and sought if he knew any, and found none. And he said: "Blessed are you, O Lord; for a great trance is fallen upon me. And he went again out of the city afar off, and abode mourning; and where he would go, he knew not."
5.8: And he set down that basket of figs, and said: "I will abide here, until the Lord take this trance from me. And after he had sat, he saw an old man coming from the field. And Abimelech said to him: To you I speak, you old man: which is this city? And the old man said to him: This is Jerusalem."
5.9: And Abimelech said to him: "Where is Jeremiah the priest, and Baruch the Levite, and all the people of this city? for I have found none. And the old man said to him: Are you not of this city? and do you remember Jeremiah even now, that you ask concerning him after all this time?"
5.10: But Jeremiah is in Babylon with the people; for they were taken captive, and delivered into the hand of Nebuchadnezzar the king of Persia; and he went there to prophesy to them.
5.11: And when Abimelech heard this from the old man, Abimelech said to him: "If you were not an old man, I would laugh you to scorn; but it is not meet that men should mock an old man; and were it not so, [I would show you]."
5.12: But as for that you say, that the people were taken captive into Babylon — though the floods of heaven had descended upon them, there has not been time for them to go into Babylon; and you say the people were taken captive into Babylon!
5.13: And I, as my father Jeremiah sent me, went into the vineyard of Agrippa for a few figs, to give to the sick that are among the people. I went and came there, and took that which he commanded me, and returned; and as I went I found a tree, and abode under it to rest, for it was midday; and there I leaned upon the basket of figs, and slept; and I awoke, thinking I had been late, and uncovered this basket of figs, and found them dripping with milk, as when I gathered them, my chosen ones. And you say the people were taken captive into Babylon!
5.14: But behold, see that my figs are not withered. And he uncovered for him the basket of figs, and showed him; and the old man looked, and Behold, the figs were fresh, and their milk dripping.
5.15: Then that old man marvelled, and said to Abimelech: "You are righteous, my son; for God would not that you should see the destruction of the city, and God brought this trance upon you, and kept you alive. Behold, it is sixty and six years this day since the people were taken captive into Babylon."
5.16: And if you will know and be sure, my son, look and see in your field that the crops have not put forth their increase, and that it is not the season for my figs; and know that the time is not the time for all this.
5.17: Then Abimelech cried with a loud voice, saying: "I bless you, O Lord my God; the God of heaven and earth; the rest of the souls of the righteous in all the world."
5.18: And he said to the old man: "What month is this? And he said to him: The tenth and second of the month Nisan, which is Miyazya. And after this Abimelech gave to that old man of these figs, and said to him: God lighten your way to the city above, Jerusalem."

6.1: And Abimelech arose, and went forth out of the city, and prayed to the Lord; and behold, an angel came and led him to Baruch, and he found him abiding in the tomb.
6.2: And when they knew each other, and had wept between themselves, and kissed one another, he saw the figs in his basket; and he lifted up his eyes to heaven, and prayed, saying:
6.3: Great is God, who givs their reward to his righteous. Rejoice, my soul, and be glad, saying to the tabernacle of flesh, O holy house; and your shall be turned into light; and after this the Faithful One coms, and shall bring you into your tabernacle. Abide in your own virgin faith, and believe, and you shall live.
6.4: Behold these figs: Behold, sixty and six years since they were gathered, and they are not withered nor rotten, but their milk dripps until this day. So shall it be done to you, my flesh, for you have kept your commandment from the angel of righteousness; who kept the basket of figs, the same shall again keep you by his power.
6.5: And when Baruch had thus spoken, he turned to Abimelech and said: "Arise, let us pray again, that the Lord may show us the words which we shall write to Jeremiah in Babylon, concerning the shelter wherewith he sheltered me."
6.6: And Baruch prayed, and said: "My strength, O God, the Lord, and the light that proceeds out of his mouth: I beseech you for your chosen. Great is your name, and there is none that can know it. Listen to the prayer of your servant, that may be manifest in my heart, your will to do; and prosper your priest Jeremiah in Babylon."
6.7: And while he was praying this, an angel came and said to him: "Baruch, minister of light, be not anxious how you shall send to Jeremiah; for at the hour of light an eagle shall come to you, and do you send him concerning Jeremiah; and write in a book, and say to them thus:"
6.8: To the children of Israel: as for the stranger that is among you, let him be set apart until fifteen days; and after this I will bring you into the city, says the Lord.
6.9: He that is not set apart in fifteen [days] from Babylon Jeremiah into the city; and the men of Babylon, says the Lord.
6.10: And when the angel had said this, he departed from Baruch. And Baruch sent to the market, and brought papyrus and ink, and wrote, saying:
6.11: By Baruch the servant of God. He writs a book to Jeremiah in the captivity of Babylon.
6.12: Rejoice and be glad; for God has not forsaken us in affliction and desolation; therefore the Lord remembered us for our tears, and remembered the covenant which he made of old with our fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
6.13: And he sent his angel to me, and told me these words which I send to you. These are the words which the Lord, the God of Israel, spoke, who brought us out of the land of Egypt: "Because you kept not all his righteousnesses, but lifted up your glory and were haughty before him, he delivered you into the furnace of Babylon, because you listened not to my word, says the Lord God, by the mouth of Jeremiah his prophet."
6.14: Them that hear, I will bring out of Babylon; and they shall not be strangers from Jerusalem in Babylon. And if you will know them and prove them, prove them by the water of Jordan; and he that hearkens not shall be by this sign, this which the great seal

7.1: And Baruch arose and went forth from the tomb, and found the eagle sitting without.
7.2: And the eagle said to him: "Hail, Baruch, steward of the faith. And Baruch said to him: For you are chosen above all the birds of heaven, that you speak; by the brightness of your eyes it is manifest; and now show me what you do here."
7.3: And the eagle said to him: "I am sent here, that you may send by me every word which you will."
7.4: And Baruch said to him: "Can you indeed bring this word to Jeremiah in Babylon? And the eagle said to him: For this was I sent."
7.5: And Baruch took the book, and fifteen figs from the basket of figs which Abimelech brought, and bound them upon the neck of the eagle.
7.6: And he said: "To you I speak, O eagle, king of all birds: go in peace and in safety; carry the message for me; and be not like the raven which Noah sent forth, and it returned not again to him; but be like the dove which the third time brought word to Noah. So do you also take these good words to Jeremiah, and to them that are with him, the Israelites, that it may be well with you; and take this gladness to the people, the chosen of God."
7.7: And if all the birds surround you, and all the enemies of righteousness, desiring to kill you, be strong; and the Lord shall give you strength. And turn not aside to the right nor to the left, but as a flying arrow go straight; go in the strength of God.
7.8: And when Baruch had said this, the eagle flew with the book, and went into Babylon; and rested upon a post without the city, in a desert place; and abode there until Jeremiah passed by, and some of the people.
7.9: And they passed by there to bury a man that was dead; for Jeremiah had asked Nebuchadnezzar, saying: Give me a place where I may bury [my dead] of my people; and he gave it him.
7.10: And as they went weeping for him that was dead, they came before that eagle; and the eagle cried with a loud voice, saying: "To you I speak, Jeremiah, chosen of God: go and gather all the people, and bring them here, that they may hear the good message which I have brought."
7.11: And when he heard this, he glorified God; and then he gathered all the people, and their wives, and their children, and they came where the eagle was.
7.12: And that eagle came down upon the corpse, and it revived and lived; and this he did that they might believe. And all the people marvelled because of that which was done.
7.13: And they said: "Of a truth this is God, who appeared to our fathers in the wilderness by Moses; and in the likeness of an eagle he appeared to us, as it were a great eagle."
7.14: And the eagle said to Jeremiah, saying: "Come, loose this book, and read it to the people; and he read it to them."
7.15: And when the people heard it, they wept all together, and cast ashes upon their heads; and they said to Jeremiah: "Save us; what shall we do, that we may enter into our city?"
7.16: And Jeremiah arose and said to them: "All that you have heard in the book, so do; and he shall bring you into your city."
7.17: And Jeremiah wrote a book to Baruch, saying thus: My beloved son, be not weary in prayer, beseeching God for us; that he may lighten our way, until we come out from under the command of this sinful king.
7.18: And you are found righteous before God, who suffered you not to come with us, that you should not see the evil that is done to them, to the people in Babylon.
7.19: As a father who has an only son, and he is delivered up to be punished; and they that are with his father, even they that comfort him, cover their faces, that they may not see the father, who is consumed with grief.
7.20: Even so God had pity on you, and suffered you not to come to Babylon, that you should not see the affliction of the people.
7.21: For since we came into this land, we have had no rest from grief until this day, sixty and six years this day; when we go forth we find of the people some hanged by Nebuchadnezzar the king, weeping and saying: Have mercy upon us, O god of Sor.
7.22: And when I heard this word, I mourned and wept, because the hanged called upon a strange god, saying: "Have mercy upon us. And again I remembered the feasts which we kept in Jerusalem, before we were taken captive; and when I remembered, I entered into my house, crying and weeping."
7.23: And now make supplication to our God, where you are, you and Abimelech, for the people, that they may listen to my voice and to the word of my mouth, that they may go out from Persia.
7.24: And now I tell you: all the time that we have abode here, they have held us, saying: Sing us new songs from the hymns of Zion, the song of your God. And we say to them: How shall we sing to you, while we are in a strange land?
7.25: And when Jeremiah had thus written, he bound his book upon the neck of the eagle, and said to him: "Go in peace, and may the Lord keep you."
7.26: And the eagle went and flew, and brought the book to Baruch; and Baruch took it and read the book, and wept when he heard of the afflictions of the people and their tribulations.
7.27: And Jeremiah took those figs, and gave them to the sick that were among the people; and abode teaching them, that they should not do the deeds of the people of Babylon.

8.1: And when the day came in which God brought the people out of Babylon, and the Lord said to Jeremiah: "Arise, you and your people, and come to Jordan, and say to the people: Let him that lovs the Lord forsake the works of the people of Babylon."
8.2: And as for the men that took wives from among you, and the women that took [husbands] from them, let us prove them.
8.3: And them that listen to you, bring you into Jerusalem; but them that listen not to you, suffer them not to enter with you.
8.4: And Jeremiah thus read to them all this, and brought them to Jordan to prove them.
8.5: And as he told them this word which the Lord spoke, they that had taken wives murmured, and would not listen to Jeremiah; and there were some that said: "We will not forsake our wives forever; we will take them with us into our city."
8.6: And they crossed over Jordan, and came into Jerusalem.
8.7: And Jeremiah and Baruch and Abimelech stood up, saying: Let no man that took [a wife] from Babylon enter into our city.
8.8: And they said to them that had taken wives for themselves: "Arise, let us go into Babylon. And they departed and went."
8.9: And when the men of Babylon saw them, they went forth, that they should not receive them, and suffered them not to enter into Babylon, saying: You are our enemies from of old; and secretly you departed from us. And for this cause you shall not enter into our city; for we have sworn by the name of our god that you and your children shall not, for secretly you departed from us.
8.10: And when they heard this, they returned into Jerusalem, and built for them a town in the districts of Jerusalem; and they called that city Samaria.
8.11: And Jeremiah sent to them, saying: Repent; and behold, the angel of righteousness shall come, and shall bring you into your place.

9.1: And they abode rejoicing and offering sacrifice seven days for the people.
9.2: And when the tenth day was come, after this was done, Jeremiah offered sacrifice alone.
9.3: And Jeremiah prayed, saying: "Holy, holy, holy are you, the sweet fragrance to men, and the light of truth, which enlighten me until I come before you."
9.4: I beseech you for your people, and I ask you for the sake of the voice of the seraphim, and for the sake of the sweet fragrance of the cherubim.
9.5: I ask you, indeed, Michael, the angel of righteousness, who I beseech you, O Lord of all, and Lord of all, who and did create all, who and, who did finish all, and all creation before they were made in secret.
9.6: And when he had prayed this, and finished his prayer, Jeremiah stood up in the temple, and with him Baruch and Abimelech; and Jeremiah became as one whose soul had gone forth from him.
9.7: And then fell Baruch and Abimelech, and cried with a loud voice, saying: "Woe to us, our father Jeremiah, the priest of God, is departed from us."
9.8: And when the people heard this, they ran to him, and found Jeremiah fallen and dead; and they wept, and rent their garments, and cast ashes upon their heads, and wept with bitter weeping.
9.9: And after they had prepared that in which they should bury him, there came a voice saying: Bury him not; he is alive, and his soul shall enter into his body again.
9.10: And when they heard this voice, they buried him not; but abode watching him three days, until his soul should enter into his body.
9.11: And there was a voice in the midst of them all, saying: Praise you with one voice, praise God; and praise you all the Messiah, the Son of God, who you and you, Jesus, the Son of God, the light of all the world, and the that fails not, and the life of faith.
9.12: And it shall be after three hundred and three weeks of time for his coming into the land, the tree of life that was in the garden, and was not planted, shall to every tree that brings forth fruit.
9.13: That they may come to him, and them, that they may bring forth fruit, and; and their fruit shall abide with the angels.
9.14: And for the planting of his tree, that they may and, to the air, that their roots may not wither, as a plant whose root has not taken hold of the earth.
9.15: And the red shall ascend as wool; and sweet water shall become bitter, and bitter shall become sweet, with great gladness.
9.16: And the rejoicings of God for the that they may bring forth fruit by the word of his mouth, his Son.
9.17: And he in the night shall enter into the world, and shall choose to him twelve apostles, that they may see that I have seen which was sent from his Father, who coms into the world, and upon the mount of Olives he shall and the soul.
9.18: And thus spoke Jeremiah concerning the Son of God, that he should come into the world.
9.19: And when the people heard this, they marvelled concerning this, and said: "This is the word of Isaiah the son of Amoz, who says: I have seen God, the Son of God."
9.20: Now arise, let us do to him as we did to Isaiah. And they said:; with a stone let us stone him.
9.21: And Baruch and Abimelech cried to them, saying: "With this death you shall not kill him."
9.22: And Baruch and Abimelech mourned for Jeremiah, and they suffered not the hidden things which he saw.
9.23: And Jeremiah said to them: "weep not; for they cannot kill me, until I make known to you all that I have seen."
9.24: And now bring you to me one stone, and bring you to him one stone; and he set it up and said: "O light of eternity, this stone, that the likeness of man may be."
9.25: And then the stone became in the likeness of Jeremiah.
9.26: And they took and stoned the stone, supposing it was Jeremiah.
9.27: And Jeremiah made known to Baruch and Abimelech all the hidden things which he saw; and after he had finished telling them, he went and stood in the midst of the people that he might finish.
9.28: And then that stone cried to them, saying: "O you lost children of Israel, why do you stone me, supposing me to be Jeremiah? And Jeremiah, behold, stands in the midst of you."
9.29: And when they saw, they ran with many stones, and upon him, and buried him; and they took that stone, and placed it in his tomb, and it as a door, and wrote in it, saying: Behold, this is the helper of Jeremiah.
